name: @test-cabinet/simple-3d
description: The Simple 3D engine: the runtime a produced 3D game is built on. An engine is created over a canvas and bound to one game, and it owns the frame loop and its replaceable clock, the letterboxed device-pixel-ratio-aware canvas fit and the frustum camera projection that maps world units into it, named input actions over keyboard bindings and touch layouts, a pointer mapped into the game's logical coordinates, an audio cue bus with its first-gesture unlock, asset loading for meshes, textures, materials, and audio under a fixed root, a diagnostics overlay, the debug surface a game returns beside its state, the write-only WebGL2 scene context the game draws through with its render modes, lights, bitmap-face HUD lettering, and the draw-command recorder inside it whose recordings replay the frames a build drew — leaving the game to write only its own simulation and rendering. Everything it does is observed by subscribing to its events rather than by reading a log it accumulates.
